item.title: Pulse Laser Deposited GaFeO3 Thin Film Grown on FTO: Correlated Ferroic Orders and Strong Magnetodielectric Coupling at Room Temperature
item.description: arXiv:2610.39696v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Room-temperature single-phase multiferroics exhibiting coupled ferroelectric and magnetic order are promising candidates for next-generation magnetoelectric memory and spintronic technologies. Here, we report the growth of approximately 100.6 nm thick polycrystalline orthorhombic GaFeO3 thin films on fluorine-doped tin oxide-coated glass (FTO) substrates by pulsed laser deposition. Core-level X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals a reduced Fe2+ concentration and suppressed oxygen-vacancy formation, contributing to reduced leakage current and improved ferroelectric characteristics. The films exhibit robust ferrimagnetism and ferroelectricity at room temperature, confirming the coexistence of ferroic orders within a single phase. Piezoresponse Force Microscopy further demonstrates reversible local polarization switching, accompanied by an asymmetric butterfly loop with coercive voltages of -0.31 V and +1.07 V. The films also exhibit a high relative dielectric constant of approximately 1700 with a relatively low dielectric loss tangent of approximately 2.83 at 1 MHz. Moreover, a significant magnetodielectric coefficient of approximately 2.3% is observed under a relatively small magnetic field of only 0.1 kOe, highlighting strong magnetoelectric coupling. These results establish GaFeO3 thin films as a promising platform for room-temperature multifunctional devices, mainly low-field magnetoelectric memory and spintronic architectures.
item.dc:creator: Ishita Jana, Sourav Sarkar, Soham Saha, Kalyan Mandal

item.title: Ghosts in the nanomachine: dynamical slowing-down in the phase-space of nanomechanical strings
item.description: arXiv:2610.39968v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The linear behavior of micro- and nanomechanical devices has been the topic of intense study over the past years. Their nonlinear behavior, on the other hand, continues to provide new and interesting dynamics. This work leverages a cavity opto-mechanical system whose very high sensitivity and low dissipation rate allows to capture the dynamics of fast transients that occur when strongly-driven nonlinear resonators relax to their equilibrium state. We experimentally study the ringdown dynamics of a nanomechanical Duffing resonator in both the time domain and in phase space. The resonator exhibits very different ringdown dynamics depending on whether it is subject to one or two tone driving. In the former case the ringdown follows a regular exponential decay, whereas the latter case shows exotic dynamics such as libration, slowing-down while scattering in phase-space, and ghost slowing-down. We demonstrate that this distinct difference can be attributed to the structure of the phase space itself. Surprisingly, we find that the energy in the resonator changes non-monotonously and that long delay between turning off the drive and the decay of the motion amplitude results in dynamical meta-states.
item.dc:creator: Samer Houri, Agnes Zinth, Menno Poot

item.title: A physics-informed uncertainty-aware surrogate for $p$-$n$ junction diodes
item.description: arXiv:2610.39993v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop an uncertainty-aware physics-informed surrogate for a one-dimensional $p$-$n$ junction diode, conditioned on device length, doping and bias. Using the internal state of the device as predicted by the surrogate we develop a test-suite of quantities of interest including the terminal current, depletion width, peak field and stored charge. The formalism and the quantities are can be extended to asymmetric junction and two-dimensional diodes as shown by means of benchmark analysis. For the one-dimensional symmetric junction surrogate, we obtain 0.11% median $L_1$ error on the electrostatic potential, and 1.5% and 0.61% on the electron and hole densities. Finally, we develop an uncertainty analysis which determines the validity of surrogate answer within the user-specified tolerance.
item.dc:creator: Suchita Kulkarni

item.title: Electrochemical functionalization of graphene rationalized by Hammett and Swain-Lupton parameters
item.description: arXiv:2610.39997v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Graphene's sp^{2}-bonded carbon lattice makes it exceptionally resistant to covalent functionalization, with existing approaches relying on chemically specific and often harsh methods, fragmenting our understanding of its reactivity. Here we show that electric fields of approximately 1 V nm^{-1} in non-aqueous electrolytes enable the electrochemical functionalization of monolayer graphene with a broad range of substituents, leading to two-order-of-magnitude conductance modulation stable over 5,000 cycles and semi-reversible electronic conductor-insulator transitions. Analysis of the oxidation potentials across substituents reveals trends governed by classical descriptors. Species forming localised {\sigma} bonds display increasing oxidation potentials with the meta-Hammett constant ({\sigma}_m), whereas substituents interacting via delocalised {\pi} orbitals follow an inverse dependence on the modified Swain-Lupton resonance parameter (R). These relationships indicate that graphene's oxidation potential increases with the electron-withdrawing strength of the substituent. Our results provide new insights into the electrochemical activity of inert materials under strong electric fields.
item.dc:creator: L. Chen, H. Li, C. Li, X. Zhang, Q. Dai, M. Alhashmi, J. Tong, E. Hoenig, Y. Li, A. Campbell, K. Hu, Y. -C. Soong, C. Sevik, L. F. Vega, F. M. Peeters, M. Lozada-Hidalgo

item.title: Scale-free wave localization at topological multicriticality
item.description: arXiv:2610.40125v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spatial wave localization at boundaries is conventionally restricted to exponential decay. Here, we observe a scale-free boundary mode exhibiting anomalous polynomial decay, highlighted by strictly linear spatial envelopes, driven by topological multicriticality in acoustic metamaterials. We establish a universal geometric bulk-boundary correspondence rooted in singularity theory by mapping n-th order topological multicriticality onto Arnold An catastrophe. We prove that defectiveness in the spatial transfer matrix enforces a (n-1)-th power spatial decay of boundary modes. At a topological tri-critical point, the singularity of winding function manifests as an A2 fold catastrophe. This dictates a strictly linear spatial decay, marking a sharp departure from the conventional exponential scaling paradigm. Using acoustic metamaterial platforms tuned to a tricritical point, we experimentally demonstrate this linear decay envelope in 1D, and further generalize it to two-dimensional systems to realize scale-free corner modes with simultaneous linear decay along orthogonal directions. While existing critical topology frameworks rely on entanglement spectra to diagnose mode existence in gapless regimes, our work bridges catastrophe theory with topological matter at multicriticalities, advancing the field from abstract mode identification to deterministic real-space wavefunction engineering.
item.dc:creator: Zhijie Xue, Yuan Tian, Nanyu Chen, Xiujuan Zhang, Tao Li, Shuang Zhang, Fuxin Guan

item.title: Topological Quantum Spin Liquids in a Ladder with Majorana fermions and p-wave Superconductivity
item.description: arXiv:2610.40297v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this article, we address the possibility of topological quantum spin liquids with only short-range (spin) correlations in the whole phase diagram in a ladder system, through an exactly solvable model which represents a generalization of the two-dimensional Kitaev honeycomb spin model to a ribbon geometry. This system gives rise to $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge fields emerging in a static way in the ground state through Majorana fermions which then produce either $0$ or $\pi$ flux. Through a quantum field theory perspective, mathematical and Density Matrix Renormalization Group results, we present our progress on the geometrical, topological and physical classification of this model through observables navigating on the whole phase diagram presenting three spin-liquid phases with a spin gap and a metallic phase in the sense of Majorana fermions. We propose a bulk-edge correspondence revealing the presence of protected zero-energy Majorana fermions at the edge in the phases with a gap and revealing also the presence of itinerant Majorana fermions in the bulk in the topological liquid phase. The proposed approach allows us to distinguish between properties of the brickwall ladder giving rise to a special line and those of the square ladder allowing for the gapless Majorana liquid phase. This model gives some hope on finding solutions for topological quantum spin models, e.g. with $\pi$ flux, on a square lattice geometry. This approach also allows for a correspondence onto models of topological superconductivity.
item.dc:creator: Magali Korolev, Fan Yang, Erik S. S{\o}rensen, Karyn Le Hur

item.title: Chiral $p$-Wave Superconductivity Proximate to a Fractional Chern Insulator and a Topological Charge Density Wave in a Moir\'e Chern Band
item.description:
arXiv:2610.40469v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a spin-polarized moir'e Chern band of twisted MoTe$_2$ with short-range repulsion, finding superconductivity proximate to a fractional Chern insulator at filling $
u=2/3$ and a topological charge density wave at $
u=3/4$. Exact diagonalization reveals pair binding over $0.7\lesssim
u\lesssim0.77$, consistent with experiment, along with finite superfluid stiffness, chiral $p$-wave pairing correlations, and adiabatic connectivity to an attractive model. At weak repulsion, Kohn-Luttinger theory supports a Fermi-surface instability with the same pairing symmetry. The superconducting state has a Bogoliubov-de Gennes Chern number $C_{\mathrm{BdG}}=-1$, opposite to the normal-state Chern number at $
u=1$. Our results reveal interplay among superconductivity, fractional topology, and charge order.
item.dc:creator: Yunze Ouyang, Fengcheng Wu

item.title: Odd Elasticity in Strain-Gradient Continua: Anisotropy Classification and Non-Hermitian Elastodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.40581v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Odd elasticity extends continuum mechanics to active nonconservative systems containing internal energy sources, such as robotic active metamaterials with nonreciprocal feedback. Modeling these systems as effective continua requires relaxing Maxwell-Betti reciprocity, which results in stiffness tensors lacking major symmetry. In this contribution, we extend this framework to 3D strain-gradient odd elasticity to incorporate the length scales inherent in these heterogeneous systems. By applying the full hierarchy of 3D point-group symmetries along chiral and achiral branches, we derive the exhaustive set of fourth-, fifth-, and sixth-order odd elastic stiffness tensors. Further, utilizing the dynamic principle of virtual work, we formulate the equilibrium equations, higher-order boundary conditions, and the generalized acoustic tensor for elastodynamic analysis. The results demonstrate that nonreciprocal moduli survive even under full isotropy in the sixth-order stiffness, under hemitropy in the fifth-order stiffness, and under cubic symmetry in fourth-order stiffness. In contrast, the elastodynamic analysis reveals that under isotropic and hemitropic limits, despite the underlying odd stiffness moduli, the acoustic tensor remains unconditionally Hermitian. Non-Hermitian elastodynamics is shown to require anisotropy. By numerically analyzing a transversely hemitropic odd elastic continuum, we demonstrate that this symmetry reduction results in non-Hermitian elastodynamic phenomena including exceptional points in the dispersion spectra and active energy exchange through simultaneous amplification and attenuation of the elastic wave components. These results provide the necessary theoretical foundation for future multiscale homogenization frameworks for anisotropic strain-gradient active microstructures, and for the design of nonreciprocal strain-gradient metamaterials.
item.dc:creator: Payam Poorsolhjouy

item.title: Probing fluctuations in photon emission statistics of spin injected quantum dots with time dependent electronic excitation
item.description: arXiv:2610.40593v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Electrically spin-injected ensembles of InGaAs/GaAs quantum dots emit circularly polarized single photons, with the emission helicity determined by the spin polarization of the injected electrons. A ferromagnetic CoFeB spin-injection layer with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, combined with an MgO tunnel barrier, enables spin-polarized electron injection into the quantum-dot active region, resulting in circularly polarized photon emission at zero applied magnetic field. These devices realize direct spin-charge-photon conversion in an electrically driven, microelectronics-compatible quantum light source that operates without an external pump laser. Using an extended Hanbury Brown-Twiss interferometer with four detectors and time-tagged readout, we measure time-resolved photon-number statistics that resolve up to $|2\rangle$ Fock states within a single excitation cycle. While single-photon ($n=|1\rangle$) emission tracks the electrical excitation pulse as expected, the two-photon ($n=|2\rangle$) statistics exhibit pronounced fluctuations at multiple temporal positions within the pulse. These fluctuations vanish upon demagnetization of the spin-injection layer, establishing a direct link between the multi-photon emission dynamics and the spin polarization of the injected carriers. The observations indicate that spin injection controls not only the helicity of the emitted photons but also higher-order temporal correlations of the emission. The behavior is phenomenologically captured by inserting both a variable excitation mechanism and a set of multi-emitter collapse operators within a stochastic wave function evolution. The platform thus opens a route to electrically driven, spin-controlled single and multi-photon Fock-state sources and provides a testbed for spin-conditioned multi-emitter dynamics in solid-state quantum light sources.
item.dc:creator: Chiran Wijesundara, Vincent Iglesias-Cardinale, Yuan Lu, Herbert Fotso, Bo Xu, Tim Thomay

item.title: Exceptional Points as Witnesses of Non-Gaussian Noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.40612v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Efficient control of quantum devices requires the knowledge of their environmental noise, yet the commonly measured power spectrum does not fully characterize non-Gaussian fluctuations of realistic environments. Here we show that exceptional points (EPs) in the noise-averaged dephasing response can expose observable signatures of non-Gaussian statistics, distinguishing environments with identical lower-order statistics. We also introduce a theoretical model that describes dephasing environments in terms of identical independent noise sources while preserving the power spectrum. Given a calibrated single-source model, the largest EP order extracted from the measured dephasing response determines the number of sources and predicts the higher-order statistics of the combined noise. We illustrate an atomtronic readout that maps distinct EP signatures onto an evolving ensemble-averaged atomic interference pattern. Our results connect non-Hermitian dynamics to environmental noise statistics, providing a route to characterize noise in quantum devices used in computing, metrology, and precision measurement.
item.dc:creator: Aritra Ghosh, Subhashish Banerjee, M. Bhattacharya

item.title: Variational wavefunctions for ideal anyon gas: superfluid and skyrmion Hall crystal
item.description: arXiv:2610.40657v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The ground state of an ideal gas of anyons with statistical angle $\theta\in(0,\pi)$ is a long-standing open problem, with renewed interest from the recent observations of fractional Chern insulators. In this work we construct variational wavefunctions that build in the exact anyon statistics and combine theory-guided composite-boson, composite-fermion and parton wavefunctions with neural-network correlations on the sphere. For spinless and SU(2) semions we confirm the paired anyon superfluid, well below the best crystal states. At $\theta=\pi/3$ liquids and crystals are closer in energy for the spinless case. For $\theta=\pi/3$ anyons with SU(3) flavor, we find two candidates. One is a skyrmion Hall crystal, in which the anyons form an integer quantum Hall state in the effective magnetic field from the spin texture. The other is a chiral color superconductor of six-anyon clusters, the color-flavor-locked pairing descendant of a holon metal with SU(3) color gauge symmetry and SU(3) flavor symmetry; its wavefunction is a hyperdeterminant rather than a product of parton determinants. Within our variational ansatz the color superconductor has better energy than both crystals and the color-flavor locked phases with U(1)$^2$ and Z$_3$ gauge groups. For twisted MoTe$_2$ this suggests that the reentrant integer quantum anomalous Hall phase is the skyrmion Hall crystal of the doped anyons, and that the observed superconductivity may be the color superconductor, which can undergo a transition to an $f+if$ BCS superconductor with a jump of the chiral central charge by 3.
item.dc:creator: Ya-Hui Zhang

item.title: GAnnET: A principled approach to automatically annotating charge stability diagrams
item.description: arXiv:2312.11206v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Gate-defined semiconductor quantum-dot (QD) arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing. However, their large configuration spaces and inherent measurement noise make device tuning time consuming and difficult to scale. Although machine-learning (ML) approaches for automated tuning have proliferated rapidly, a fair comparison of methods remains limited by inconsistent metrics and a lack of standardized labeled datasets. Here, we introduce Geometry-Informed ANNotator for Electrostatic Topologies (GAnnET), a physics- and geometry-informed algorithm that automatically generates probabilistic state labels for charge stability diagrams (CSDs) of double-QD systems. GAnnET constructs local geometric models of CSD structure and combines them into a global state map with calibrated confidence, eliminating the need for manual annotation. We validate GAnnET on simulated and experimental CSDs and demonstrate consistent labeling suitable for ML training and benchmarking. By enabling reproducible annotation of experimental data, GAnnET supports community benchmarking and scalable automated QD operation.
item.dc:creator: Brian Weber, Justyna P. Zwolak

item.title: Quantum Hall transformer in a quantum point contact over the full range of transmission
item.description: arXiv:2406.17778v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A recent experiment [Cohen et al., Science 382, 542 (2023)] observed a robustly quantized $e^2/2h$ conductance in a quantum point contact between fractional quantum Hall edges (a quantum Hall transformer), which then vanishes at low temperature. While this behavior can be described by a boundary sine gordon (BSG) model derived from electron tunneling, the microscopic motivation for such strong tunneling is unclear. We use an alternative model based on sliding charge density waves and a density inhomogeneity to clarify the BSG description and calculate the conductance over the full range of transmission. Using a perturbative method and a matrix product state calculation, we draw a quantitative connection between the BSG model and the physical quantum Hall system.
item.dc:creator: Stuart Yi-Thomas, Jay D. Sau

item.title: Computational quantum transport: a scattering approach perspective
item.description: arXiv:2407.16257v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This review is devoted to the different techniques that have been developed to compute the phase-coherent transport properties of quantum nanoelectronic systems connected to electrodes. Beside a review of the different algorithms proposed in the literature, we provide a comprehensive and pedagogical derivation of the two formalisms on which these techniques are based: the scattering approach and the (nonequilibrium) Green's function approach. We show that the scattering problem can be formulated as a system of linear equations and that different existing algorithms for solving this scattering problem amount to different sequences of Gaussian elimination. We explicitly prove the equivalence of the two formalisms. We discuss the stability and numerical complexity of the existing methods. The review ends with a selection of a few applications where numerical calculations were instrumental in shaping our understanding of the physics.
item.dc:creator: Xavier Waintal, Michael Wimmer, Anton Akhmerov, Christoph Groth, Branislav K. Nikolic, Mathieu Istas, T\'omas \"Orn Rosdahl, Daniel Varjas

item.title: Chiral Geometric Qubit in a Frustrated Molecular Spin Triangle
item.description: arXiv:2501.11964v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spin frustration in antiferromagnetically coupled triangles creates states distinguished by chirality, offering a molecular route to encoded quantum operations. Here, we show how scalar chirality and geometric phases arise in the ground doublet of a spin-$1/2$ triangle. A Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya (DM) interaction establishes the chirality of the states, while broken $C_3$ symmetry allows these states to acquire geometric phases. We show how to encode a qubit in states of opposite scalar chirality and opposite geometric phases and implement a geometric $Z$ gate that cancels the relative dynamical phase, making it insensitive to pulse-duration errors. As an example of such a chiral geometric qubit, we investigate a Cu$_3$-based paramagnetic molecular magnet, using broken-symmetry density functional theory and multireference spin--orbit calculations to estimate the strengths of the exchange and DM interactions. The results show that such paramagnetic molecules could serve as tunable platforms for implementing chiral geometric qubits.
item.dc:creator: Aman Ullah, Ziqi Hu, Juan Arag\'o, Sergey A. Varganov, Alejandro Gaita-Ari\~no

item.title: Shape dependence of Edelstein and magnetoelectric effects in the V-shaped model
item.description: arXiv:2511.14404v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We theoretically investigate the shape dependence and microscopic mechanism of the magnetoelectric (ME) effect, including both nonmagnetic (Edelstein-type) and magnetic origins, in a V-shaped one-dimensional chain model. Numerical calculations based on the Kubo formula reveal that the nonmagnetic-driven ME response is maximized at an apex angle of $\theta \approx 0.6\pi$. To clarify its origin, we derive a low-energy effective Hamiltonian in the $s$-orbital subspace and demonstrate that the polarity induced by the V-shaped geometry manifests as an effective spin--orbit interaction. An analytical derivation of the Green's function shows that the geometric effect can be described as a $T$-matrix contribution associated with local symmetry breaking. This scattering-theoretical representation enables us to identify the contributions of local geometric symmetry breaking to the ME response. Using a multipole-basis representation, we identify symmetry-based selection rules for the ME tensor and show that the coupling between the effective spin--orbit interaction and the orbital angular momentum generated across the apex plays an essential role. The resulting angular dependence, $\sin{\theta}\sin{\theta/2}$, peaks at $\theta = 2\tan^{-1}\sqrt{2} \approx 0.608\pi$, in good agreement with the numerical results. We also analyze a ferromagnetic V-shaped model including the Zeeman interaction and show that the magnetic-driven ME response originates from the spin magnetization induced by the coupling between the electric-field--driven charge-potential gradient and the Zeeman term. These results reveal distinct ME mechanisms depending on the presence or absence of time-reversal symmetry and clarify the microscopic origin of shape-dependent ME responses in V-shaped chains.
item.dc:creator: Shuhei Kanda, Satoru Hayami

item.title: Curvature-stabilized three-dimensional spiral states and local-field nucleation of skyrmions on spherical caps
item.description: arXiv:2511.22557v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The combination of polystyrene particles and multilayers with chiral interfacial interactions offers an interesting platform to study the interplay between topology, chirality, and curvature. Here, we investigate Pt/Co/Ta multilayers sputtered onto self-assembled polystyrene particles with a diameter of 919 nm, which show a magnetic reversal distinctly different from that of planar films. Using non-invasive scanning transmission X-ray microscopy and in-vacuum magnetic force microscopy (MFM) with low-moment tips, we observe maze domains in the planar films, whereas the curvilinear films host three-dimensional spiraling stripe states. Repeated scanning with a conventional higher-moment MFM tip ruptures these spirals into metastable skyrmions at the top of the particles. Micromagnetic simulations of spherical caps reveal that increasing curvature renders a single spiral stripe energetically favorable over an isolated skyrmion, and that this stabilization is predominantly of magnetostatic origin. Our results identify the spiral states as intrinsic to the curvilinear geometry and the skyrmions as metastable states nucleated by local magnetic fields, underlining the value of non-invasive imaging to distinguish intrinsic curvature effects from probe-induced magnetic textures.
item.dc:creator: Sabri Koraltan, Joe Sunny, Emily Darwin, Daniel Rothhardt, Reshma Peremadathil-Pradeep, Micha{\l} Krupi\'nski, Takeaki Gokita, Robert Kraft, Claas Abert, Jakub Jurczyk, Amalio Fern\'andez-Pacheco, Markus Weigand, Sebastian Wintz, Dieter Suess, Hans Josef Hug, Manfred Albrecht

item.title: Kineo-Elasticity and Nonreciprocal Phonons by Rashba-induced Interfacial Spin-Lattice Coupling
item.description: arXiv:2601.12656v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We identify a previously unrecognized spin-lattice coupling allowed by broken inversion symmetry that can be viewed as a lattice analogue of electronic Rashba spin-orbit coupling. In the low-frequency regime, where magnons are integrated out, its interplay with the conventional magnetoelastic coupling generates a kineo-elastic term that couples strain and lattice velocity, giving rise to nonreciprocal phonon velocity. We further analyze the full magnon-phonon spectrum and find that the competition between interfacial spin-lattice and magnetoelastic couplings leads to directional hybridization and absorption, yielding asymmetric phonon propagation lengths for opposite directions. Our results indicate that such interfacial spin-lattice coupling can provide an efficient route to nonreciprocal phonon propagation in magnetic heterostructures with strong Rashba spin-orbit coupling.
item.dc:creator: Gyungchoon Go, Se Kwon Kim

item.title: Thermal Strain-Driven Periodic Ripples in Ultrathin Sb2Te3/Graphene Heterostructures and their Implications for Strain Engineering
item.description: arXiv:2602.11932v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report the observation of a highly regular, periodic ripple superstructure with a characteristic wavelength of approximately 8.7 nm in a van der Waals heterostructure composed of ultrathin Sb2Te3 epitaxially grown on monolayer graphene. We attribute this structural modulation to an extrinsic, thermally driven mechanism: upon post-growth cooling, the opposite signs of the thermal expansion coefficients of the bulk SiO2 substrate and the graphene layer generate interfacial strain that drives the formation of ripples. In this ultrathin thickness regime, the Sb2Te3 film conforms to the buckled graphene morphology without delamination, because the interfacial van der Waals adhesion energy exceeds the elastic energy cost associated with bending. This substrate-induced templating mechanism is expected to be broadly applicable to other two-dimensional materials grown on graphene, provided that they are sufficiently thin to remain mechanically coupled below a critical bending thickness. Furthermore, based on density functional theory and effective low-energy model calculations, we predict that this structural corrugation leads to substantial modifications of the electronic band structure. The resulting periodic ripple potential suppresses the trivial hybridization gap in the planar configuration and transforms the spinless Dirac-Dirac resonance into a gapless helical metallic state with a dense, nontrivial spin texture.
item.dc:creator: Francisco Munoz, Manuel Fuenzalida, Paula Mellado, Caleb Z. Zerger, Hari C. Manoharan, Valentina Gallardo, Carolina Parra

item.title: Increasing valley splitting in Si/SiGe by practically achievable heterostructure profiles
item.description: arXiv:2603.19769v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Silicon spin qubits are marred by the valley degeneracy of the conduction band. In a nanodevice, the degeneracy is lifted by interfaces and alloy disorder, but the resulting valley splitting is small, of order 100 $\mu$eV in Si/SiGe quantum wells. Substantial efforts were invested both in theory and experiments to overcome the valley issue. Unfortunately, the existing recipes either rely on atomistic details of the interface that are beyond experimental control, or demand heterostructure profiles beyond current state-of-the-art heterostructure epitaxy. We revisit the valley splitting induced by non-trivial Ge profiles and advocate a novel view of the intervalley coupling as backscattering on point-like impurities realized by crystal planes containing Ge atoms. This perspective reveals that enhancing the backscattering amplitude, which sets the valley splitting, requires constructive interference of multiple scatterers. % We arrive at a remarkable prediction that the Ge content along the heterostructure growth direction does not have to have any specific periodicity, including the practically unreachable $2\pi/(2k_0)$ period, to significantly increase the valley splitting. Numerical evidence from tight-binding simulations and intuitive physical interpretations corroborate this statement. We devise profiles that seem within the capabilities of current MBE growth techniques and boost the valley splitting beyond the 1\,meV scale.

item.title: Geometric assembly of topology in hybrid bosonic bands: magnon-phonon excitations in skyrmion crystals
item.description: arXiv:2604.10483v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Hybridization between bosonic excitations can produce topological bands, but their Chern numbers conceal how constituent modes generate the resulting Berry geometry. Here we derive an exact decomposition of Berry curvature in multicomponent bosonic Bogoliubov-de Gennes systems into weighted constituent-sector contributions and a term associated with single-quasiparticle entanglement. The latter couples momentum-space variations of the sector imbalance to a gauge-invariant relative Berry connection and has an equivalent gauge-covariant pseudospin representation. Applying this framework to magnon-phonon excitations in a ferromagnetic skyrmion crystal, we find that magnetoelastic coupling generates topological low-energy hybrid bands despite the trivial topology of the two lowest uncoupled magnon bands and degeneracies among folded phonons. The resulting Chern numbers are assembled through constructive, entanglement-assisted, and entanglement-compensated geometric mechanisms. In particular, bands with identical Chern numbers can exhibit opposite entanglement contributions. Our approach thus resolves nonquantized internal geometric contributions hidden within quantized hybrid-band invariants, without requiring an effective two-level Hamiltonian.
item.dc:creator: Doried Ghader, Bilal Jabakhanji

item.title: Antiferro-Chiral Phonons as Conjugate Fields to N\'eel Order in $\mathcal{P}\mathcal{T}$-Symmetric Antiferromagnets
item.description: arXiv:2605.08490v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Chiral phonons act as a phononic conjugate field to net magnetization, enabling phononic detection and control of ferromagnetic order. Whether an analogous phononic coupling exists for the compensated N\'eel order of antiferromagnets has remained open. Here we show that, in $\mathcal{P}\mathcal{T}$-symmetric antiferromagnets, phonons with sublattice-staggered angular momentum can couple to the N\'eel vector like a conjugate field. Such coupling can be induced by the molecular Berry curvature-induced gyroscopic coupling between Raman and infrared-active phonons. The gyroscopic coupling is odd under both $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{T}$ while preserving their product. $\mathcal{P}\mathcal{T}$ symmetry forbids the resulting normal modes to have a net phonon angular momentum (PAM) while allows counter-rotating local motion on inversion-related sublattices, which are dubbed the antiferro-chiral phonons (AFCPs). Reversing the N\'eel vector reverses the staggered phonon chirality and the sign of the coupling. Our results indicate AFCPs can serve as probes and control knobs of N\'eel order.

item.title: Coherent control of spinmons
item.description: arXiv:2605.12588v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we explore a hybrid qubit device where quantum information is encoded by quantum states of a transmon entangled with the spin of a trapped Andreev quasiparticle. We term such devices spinmons. We lift the spinmon Kramers degeneracy by introducing a Zeeman field and develop two routes for full qubit control via electrostatic gates and an AC flux drive, providing multiple directions for experimental implementations. Finally, we compute coherence times, verify the qubit robustness against flux, charge and gate voltage noise sources, and discuss the role of nuclear spin noise.
item.dc:creator: Johanne Bratland Tjernshaugen, Florinda Vi\~nas Bostr\"om, Jeroen Danon, Jacob Linder, Karsten Flensberg, Antonio L. R. Manesco

item.title: The Topography Trap: Sifting Interlayer Excitons from Strain-Related Artifacts in Real-World 2D Heterostructures
item.description: arXiv:2605.20869v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Novel excitonics emerging in transition metal dichalcogenide (TMDC) heterostructures belong to the most exciting topics in contemporary physics of van der Waals materials. Interlayer excitons (IXs) stand out among those due to their long radiative lifetimes and tunability by electric fields, strain, and twist angle. However, many ambiguities persist in the optical identification and manipulation of IXs, highlighting the need for reliable spectroscopic criteria that distinguish interlayer species from spurious signals. Here, we introduce a decision-tree protocol that evaluates interlayer coupling via intralayer exciton quenching and correlates photoluminescence (PL) with atomic force microscopy to establish IX-compatibility of room-temperature PL features in TMDC-based heterostructures. Applied to MoS$_2$-MoSe$_2$ and MoS$_2$-WSe$_2$ heterostructures, it recovers the established momentum-direct IX between the K valleys of the two layers (KK-IX). In WS$_2$-WSe$_2$, a low-energy feature persists through flat, well-coupled regions and for both stacking orders, supporting its assignment as IX-compatible. In contrast, we find no compelling evidence that the widely reported bright, momentum-indirect, twist-angle-independent $\Gamma$K-IX signature in MoS$_2$-WSe$_2$ originates from interlayer emission. Comprehensive experimental data, including infrared and tip-enhanced photoluminescence, stacking order inversion, interface cleaning, control measurements on WSe$_2$/Au, and statistics on variously prepared samples, instead trace these features to locally decoupled and strained WSe$_2$ at interface bubbles and topographical irregularities. Our results expose a generic "topography trap" in real-world heterostructures and establish a practical minimum standard for robust IX assignments, the sift-IX protocol, through spatially resolved room-temperature optical and topographic characterization.

item.title: Photon-energy-programmable subnanometric electron birth-site control
item.description: arXiv:2605.28286v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Optical control of electron-generation sites has broadly enabled ultrafast nanoscale imaging, spectroscopy, and functional control. Existing approaches achieve nanoscale site selectivity by shaping localised optical fields around nanostructures, thereby limiting independent site selectivity within the same local-field hotspot. Here, using a single-molecule electron emitter, we show that site selectivity can instead be encoded in the electronic excitation pathway, enabling subnanometric control of electron birth sites within a common local-field hotspot. By tuning the photon energy, we selectively access different groups of molecular states whose combined contributions define emission channels with distinct spatial character, thereby reversibly switching the electron birth site within the same emitter. The switching is read out directly in the far-field emission pattern and occurs upon changing the photon energy, but not upon varying the intensity or polarisation. Our results establish optical birth-site selectivity that is not dictated by the local-field distribution, opening a route to electron birth-site control through the electronic excitation pathway.

item.title: Phonon down-conversion by normal metals for superconducting devices
item.description: arXiv:2607.13870v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Thanks to low dissipation, superconducting devices are promising for a number of applications, such as detectors and implementations of quantum computation. However, their working can be adversely impacted by quasiparticles, which is why so-called quasiparticle poisoning mechanisms and their mitigation are under intense investigation. Here we focus on one poisoning mechanism, namely pair-breaking phonons, and its mitigation through down-conversion by a normal-metal film - the process in which scattering of high-energy phonons by electrons lowers the energy of the former below the pair-breaking threshold. To study the down-conversion, we introduce a model based on kinetic equations, which we solve both analytically (approximately) and numerically in the steady state. We use the solution to the estimate a properly-defined down-conversion efficiency which depends on material parameters (such as the strength of electron-phonon interaction and the phonon transmission coefficient at interfaces) and film and substrate thicknesses. Interestingly, we find that the efficiency is nearly optimal above a minimum metal thickness, typically between 50 and 500 nm depending on the metal-substrate combination.

item.title: Time-Reversal-Invariant Altermagnetic Acoustic Crystals
item.description: arXiv:2608.08827v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Altermagnets have emerged as a new class of magnetic materials that combine spin-split electronic bands with zero net magnetization. Extending this paradigm to classical-wave systems has, however, been fundamentally challenging because conventional realizations require broken time-reversal symmetry (TRS). Here, we overcome this limitation by introducing a pseudospin degree of freedom and constructing a pseudo-time-reversal operator that faithfully reproduces the action of its physical counterpart while preserving actual TRS. Building on this framework, we theoretically propose and experimentally realize the first time-reversal-invariant altermagnetic acoustic crystal. Acoustic measurements directly reveal pseudospin-dependent band splitting--a defining hallmark of altermagnetism--under strictly TRS-preserving conditions. Moreover, the altermagnetic acoustic crystal exhibits sublattice-pseudospin locking, enabling flexible control over acoustic pseudospin splitting and filtering. Our work establishes acoustic crystals as a versatile platform for exploring altermagnetic physics and opens new avenues for spin-inspired wave manipulation in nonmagnetic devices.

item.title: Model of the magnon Kerr effect in a highly anisotropic ferromagnet
item.description: arXiv:2609.24959v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The magnon Kerr effect is a nonlinear phenomenon that occurs universally in any ferromagnet with finite magnetic anisotropy. It manifests itself as a magnon population-dependent change in the magnon dispersion relation. Here, we derive the Hamiltonian for the magnon Kerr effect for a thin film with uniaxial anisotropy. We consider the external field, parallel, perpendicular, and at an intermediate angle to the anisotropy axis, and determine the Kerr coefficient in each case. We show how the nonlinearity scales for different magnetic materials as a function of magnon frequency and magnetic sample volume. Moreover, we derive the equations of motion for a hybrid cavity-magnon system with such thin-film magnon Kerr nonlinearity, to obtain populations of photons and magnons, and scattering matrix terms for the microwave transmission of the cavity, relevant for experimental observations.

item.title: Quantum noise spectroscopy of superconducting dynamics in a cuprate thin film
item.description: arXiv:2502.04439v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Characterizing the low-energy dynamics of quantum materials is crucial for understanding strongly correlated electronic states, yet remains experimentally challenging, particularly in two-dimensional systems. Here, we leverage nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond as a non-invasive quantum sensor to study thin-film Bi$_2$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+\delta}$ (BSCCO), revealing several distinct dynamical phenomena across the superconducting phase diagram. At zero magnetic field and low temperatures, NV depolarization ($T_1$) spectroscopy captures GHz-scale noise from nodal quasiparticle excitations, consistent with Bardeen--Cooper--Schrieffer (BCS) mean-field theory. Near the critical temperature $T_c \approx 90$ K, supercurrent-fluctuation-induced noise sharply reduces $T_1$. By analyzing the temperature scaling of $T_1$, we observe clear deviations from mean-field prediction, reflecting the importance of order parameter fluctuations and enabling the determination of critical exponents. Under a small magnetic field, a broad and asymmetric reduction of $T_1$ unveils a liquid-like phase of mobile vortices. NV decoherence ($T_2$) spectroscopy further probes MHz-scale noise and reveals complex vortex-solid fluctuations well below $T_c$. Our results establish quantum noise spectroscopy as a non-invasive probe of superconducting dynamics over frequency and length scales complementary to existing techniques.

item.title: Remotely programming the weights of a spintronic neural network by a radiofrequency broadcast signal
item.description: arXiv:2604.24561v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Selectively programming a large number of non-volatile synaptic weights without compromising scalability is a key challenge for in-memory computing. Here, we experimentally demonstrate remote programming of synaptic weights in series-connected chains of 11 vortex-based magnetic tunnel junctions using broadcast radiofrequency signals applied through a shared strip line. Because each junction is engineered with a distinct resonance frequency, programming relies on frequency-selective reversal of the vortex-core polarity and therefore does not require individual access lines or selector devices. Reconfiguring the binary states of these chains strongly reshapes the continuous spectral transfer functions that determine the weighted sums performed on frequency-multiplexed RF inputs. This allows compact networks built from such chains to process high-dimensional RF-encoded inputs. We experimentally perform handwritten-digit classification and drone RF-signature identification using a two-chain network comprising only 22 synapses in total. After remote reconfiguration for each task, the spintronic network respectively reaches 93.9 +/- 2.3 % and 99.5 +/- 1 % test accuracy, on par with the software baseline. Broadcast RF programming thus provides a compact and scalable route to rapidly reconfigurable spintronic neuromorphic hardware.

item.title: Tailoring the properties of YBa$_{2}$Cu$_{3}$O$_{7-\delta}$ thin films by 30-keV He$^+$ irradiation: An enabling route to superconducting device nanopatterning
item.description: arXiv:2606.14588v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Focused helium ion beam (He-FIB) irradiation with 30-keV ions is a key tool for nanoscale patterning and defect engineering in high transition temperature (Tc) cuprate superconducting devices, yet its usable fluence window is constrained by the competing requirements of reliable superconductivity suppression and minimal structural degradation. In this work, we provide a comprehensive dataset on the effects of large-area 30-keV He+ ion exposure on the electric transport and superconducting properties of epitaxial YBa2Cu3O7 (YBCO) thin films. X-ray diffraction shows a fluence-driven loss of crystalline order accompanied by an out-of-plane lattice expansion and an orthorhombic-to-tetragonal transition, culminating in predominant amorphization at the highest fluence of 1 x 10^16 cm^-2. Raman spectra exhibit increasing disorder while lacking signatures of oxygen depletion, indicating that irradiation mainly generates oxygen-related Frenkel defects rather than changing the carrier concentration. Consistently, with increasing fluence, the normal-state resistivity \rho_N(T) at temperature T above Tc increases strongly, while d \rho_N/d T remains nearly unchanged at moderate fluence. The suppression of Tc is accurately described by Abrikosov-Gor'kov pair breaking and reaches complete quenching of superconductivity at 4.5 x 10^15 cm^-2. The anisotropic upper critical fields decrease approximately exponentially with increasing fluence, the vortex activation energy is reduced, and the anisotropy drops, in contrast to oxygen-depleted YBCO. Hall-angle analysis confirms a nearly constant carrier density but a systematic increase in defect scattering and reduced mobility, consistent with a crossover toward the dirty limit at high fluence. These results establish quantitative fluence thresholds and a practical operational window for He-FIB nanopatterning of YBCO quantum circuits.

item.title: Wald entropy and Wen-Zee type gauge-curvature coupling in 2+1-dimensional gravity
item.description: arXiv:2610.04476v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Wen-Zee term is a mixed gauge-curvature coupling in the topological Chern-Simons description of a quantum Hall fluid, encoding the electric charge bound to spatial curvature. We investigate a Lorentz-covariant generalization of this coupling, expanding its scope to black-hole spacetimes and determine its contribution to horizon entropy. Such a coupling arises naturally in three-dimensional Chern-Simons gravity based on the Maxwell algebra. We show that its Wald entropy contribution is a horizon boost charge, given by a loop integral of the additional gauge field projected along the tangent to the bifurcation circle. This contribution can be nonzero even when the mixed term vanishes on shell. We show that the integral admits an Abelian holonomy interpretation when the projection direction is covariantly constant. We evaluate the charge on a flat cosmological solution and, using smooth horizon fields and a specified thermal ensemble, on an AdS-Lorentz black hole. These results connect the geometric response familiar from quantum Hall physics to gravitational horizon thermodynamics.
item.dc:creator: Aryan Bhatia, Giandomenico Palumbo, Suraj S. Hegde

item.title: Solving fractional quantum Hall problems with thermodynamic-limit bootstrap
item.description:
arXiv:2610.21317v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Determining correlated ground states directly in the thermodynamic limit remains a central challenge in quantum many-body physics. Here we develop a quantum many-body bootstrap that yields a rigorous and tight lower bound on the thermodynamic ground-state energy of a fractional quantum Hall system together with an optimized reduced density matrix $ho_W^\star$ on a spatial window. For sufficiently tight bounds, we find that $ho_W^\star$ accurately reproduces the ground-state reduced density matrix, as directly tested by its fidelity with known model states. For exactly solvable Laughlin and Moore--Read parent Hamiltonians, the bootstrap also reproduces pair correlations and orbital entanglement spectra (OES). For Landau-level-projected Coulomb interactions across multiple fillings, the energy bounds closely track established thermodynamic estimates, while the window density matrix recovers the familiar $
u=1/3$ Laughlin and $
u=5/2$ Moore--Read states and the composite Fermi liquid at $
u=1/2$. More importantly, the same framework also resolves unsettled regimes. At $
u=1/4$, the OES and real-space correlations identify a composite Fermi liquid, while at $
u=12/5$ the combined diagnostics suggest $\overline{\mathrm{RR}}_3$ as the ground-state order. Our bootstrap therefore provides direct access to both ground-state energies and many-body structure in the thermodynamic limit.
item.dc:creator: Qiang Gao, Taige Wang

item.title: Theory of High-Temperature Fractional Chern Phases in Monolayer van der Waals Kagome Materials A$_2$T$_3$X$_4$
item.description: arXiv:2610.24633v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Fractional Chern insulators bring the fractional quantum Hall effect, with its anyonic excitations, to zero magnetic field. So far they have been realized in moir\'e materials, where the long superlattice period weakens electronic interactions and confines these phases to cryogenic temperatures. Early proposals instead envisioned topological flat bands on atomic-scale lattices, where fractionalization could persist to far higher temperatures, but a suitable material has been lacking. Here we theoretically identify monolayers of the van der Waals kagome family $\mathrm{A}_2\mathrm{T}_3\mathrm{X}_4$ as such a platform, combining intrinsic topological flat bands and strong Coulomb interactions with gate-tunable carrier density and layer assembly. Exact diagonalization of models derived from density functional theory reveals ferromagnetism over broad filling ranges, supporting diverse fractional Chern insulators, anomalous composite Fermi liquids, and charge-ordered phases. In particular, in $\mathrm{Cs}_2\mathrm{Pd}_3\mathrm{S}_4$, the fractional Chern insulator exhibits a many-body gap of approximately 26 meV in the largest system accessible with band mixing allowing at most one interband electron-hole excitation. Layer assembly further provides a natural route to fractional quantum spin Hall insulators: bilayers with antiparallel magnetizations support this phase at realistic separations. These results identify an experimentally accessible material family in which chemical composition, carrier density, and stacking offer complementary routes to fractionalization at enhanced energy scales and control over topological order.
item.dc:creator: Soomin Oh, Jiyong Han, Jinhyeok Choi, Donghae Seo, Mingu Kang, Gil Young Cho

item.title: Mechanistic discovery in grain boundary structure and deformation driven by agentic AI
item.description: arXiv:2610.28629v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems hold immense potential for automating complex workflows in materials discovery and design, but extending these capabilities to domain-intensive mechanistic studies remains challenging. General grain boundaries (GBs) exemplify this challenge, as their structural complexity complicates experimental characterization and atomistic modeling. Here, we present GBClaw, an agentic AI framework for investigating the structure and deformation of general GBs, which are common in real polycrystals yet remain understudied. By integrating large language models into a modular architecture, GBClaw effectively combines systematic simulations with targeted mechanistic analysis through iterative workflow refinement and dynamic replanning. Applied to 14 general asymmetric tilt GBs in nickel, the framework characterized interfacial defect structures and deformation modes across these incommensurate boundaries. It established a general approach to identify previously unobserved, widely spaced secondary GB misfit dislocations (SGBMDs) alongside closely spaced primary GB misfit dislocations (PGBMDs) in simulated atomic configurations and experimental images. Comparisons of GB sliding with and without SGBMDs revealed substantial differences in shear strength, underscoring the critical role of misfit-dislocation hierarchies in sliding resistance. Researcher-guided follow-up calculations further elucidated the structural origins of shear asymmetry and an anomalous shear response. This work demonstrates that combining agentic AI with domain expertise bridges high-throughput computational screening and deep mechanistic discovery at complex material interfaces.
